Verdict

No confirmed indicators of malicious supply-chain compromise. Overall risk: **info**.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • pyproject.toml uses the standard poetry-core build backend (poetry.core.masonry.api); no evidence of custom build hooks that would execute arbitrary commands during installation was found.
  • No setup.py, .pth, sitecustomize.py, or usercustomize.py was observed in the provided files.
  • sae_lens/__init__.py performs module imports and SAE class registration, but within the reviewed content there is no evidence of suspicious import-time file/network access, credential collection, or obfuscated loader execution.
  • No evidence of malicious automatic execution via CLI/entry points was identified in the provided content.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Stealth

  • **Credential harvesting:** No evidence of broad discovery of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud credentials, CI tokens, wallets, or similar secrets.

- load_dotenv() in neuronpedia_integration.py appears related to documented use of an OPENAI_API_KEY; by itself this is not a supply-chain malware indicator.

  • **Exfiltration/staging:** No evidence of archive staging, base64 packaging, harvested-file upload, webhook use, raw IP/C2 endpoints, or stealthy transmission.

- requests.get/post usage appears to implement Neuronpedia API functionality and is not tied to credential theft or covert exfiltration in the reviewed code.

  • **Persistence:** No evidence of systemd units, cron jobs, shell profile edits, launch agents, startup folders, or self-reinstall logic.
  • **Lateral movement:** No evidence of Kubernetes token use, Docker socket access, cloud metadata probing, GitHub Actions/CI token theft, or workflow injection.
  • **Obfuscation/loader:** No evidence of eval/exec, marshal/pickle loaders, compressed/encrypted payloads, downloader stubs, or self-deleting droppers. The pre-scan “encrypted-payload” matches appear to be false positives on strings such as SAE.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • The provided metadata and file contents do not show evidence of typosquatting, hidden payloads, unexplained native binaries, abnormal .dist-info contents, or suspicious dependency insertion.
  • Dependencies such as transformer-lens, transformers, datasets, python-dotenv, and safetensors are consistent with the stated ML/SAE purpose and are not tied to malicious supply-chain behavior in the reviewed evidence.
  • The provided data is insufficient to determine whether the PyPI sdist differs from the upstream GitHub source.

Additional Verification Needed

  • The text corpus covers only selected files, so review of all 65 extracted files is limited.
  • If a wheel artifact also exists, it should be compared against the sdist for file and behavior differences.
  • Reproducibility comparison between the PyPI sdist and the upstream GitHub tag/commit was not provided and would be needed for stronger distribution-integrity assurance.
